tickets.title: P?-66: ObserveFollowerFill returns silently five different ways, so a zero in the UI is uninterpretable -- instrument every path
tickets.defect:
P1-22's slippage and latency metrics produced NO reading on the live path, and the cause is unresolved. `ObserveFollowerFill` (addons/TradeCopierEngine.cs:2671) has FIVE ways to return without recording anything, and all five leave exactly the same trace: none.

  1. `exec == null || exec.Order == null`
  2. the pending-copy lookup misses -- `_pendingCopies.TryGetValue(exec.Order, ...)` returns false
  3. `rel == null` after the relationship resolution
  4. latency computed but rejected by `latencyMs >= 0 && latencyMs < 600000`
  5. slippage skipped: `!PriceComparable || FollowerTickSize <= 0 || LeaderFillPrice <= 0 || exec.Price <= 0`

So `LatencyMs: 0.0, AvgSlippageTicks: 0.0` in the live config can mean the copy was clean, or that it was never matched, or that the relationship did not resolve, or that the reading was thrown out as absurd, or that the two instruments' prices are not comparable. A zero is not a pass. This is the same class of defect P1-22 itself was: a displayed figure that nothing computes reads as evidence the copy was clean.

THE TWO LIVE SUSPECTS. (a) The pending map is keyed on the follower `Order` OBJECT REFERENCE -- which is correct, since NT8's OrderId is neither unique nor stable -- but that means anything handing back a different instance measures nothing and says nothing. That is the P0-59/P3-30 shape. (b) `exec.Time`'s DateTimeKind is not dependable, and a leader timestamp in a different frame from the follower's yields a latency of several hours, which the sanity bound then correctly and silently discards.

RULED OUT by inspection on 2026-08-13, so do not spend the ticket on it: the 'group-derived relationship is a fresh object from ToRelationships()' hypothesis. The live CopierConfig has `Groups: {}` and two direct entries under `Relationships`, so `_relationships` does contain the pair and `rel` resolves.
tickets.spec:
Make each of the five outcomes emit a DISTINCT log line through the existing `CopierLog(account, eventType, message)` helper, and emit one on the success path too.

1. THE SUCCESS PATH FIRST. Log `FILL_MEASURED` when a fill is matched and measured, carrying the latency in ms and the slippage in ticks. Without the positive case an absent log line cannot be told from a log line that was never reached, so the misses below prove nothing on their own. The acceptance test requires the numbers to appear in the message text.

2. `FILL_NOT_MEASURED` when the pending-copy lookup misses. Include whatever identifies the order to a human reading the live log -- its name, and its OrderId with the standing caveat that the id is display-only here and must NEVER become the map key.

3. `LATENCY_REJECTED` when a latency is computed and then thrown out by the sanity bound. Name the figure it refused and both timestamps, because that is the evidence that decides between a real clock skew and a DateTimeKind mismatch. DO NOT change the bound, do not 'fix' the timestamps, and do not start converting one side -- converting one side only would inject the UTC offset as latency, which is what the existing comment at the latency calculation warns about. Recording the rejection is the entire ask.

4. `SLIPPAGE_NOT_COMPARABLE` when the price check declines to compute slippage. Say which of the conditions failed -- an incomparable root pairing and a zero tick size are different problems with different fixes.

5. The `rel == null` path, and the `exec.Order == null` path, get lines too. The first has no acceptance test because it is not currently reachable with the live config shape; instrument it anyway, since the whole point of the ticket is that an unreachable-looking path is exactly what the last one turned out to be.

CONSTRAINTS:
- BEHAVIOUR MUST NOT CHANGE. Same measurements, same recorded values, same sanity bound, same quarantine decision, same entry-only asymmetry (a quarantined relationship still copies EXITS -- blocking those strands the follower in a position the leader has left, which is P0-5 by another route). This ticket adds observation, nothing else.
- These lines are on the fill path of every copy, so they are hot. Keep them to one line per outcome; do not add a line per branch inside a loop.
- ASCII only, and `CopierLog` is already the dual sink that reaches both the Output tab and RiskGuard's structured log. Do not call `Output.Process` directly.
tickets.context:
`ObserveFollowerFill` is called from `OnExecution` at addons/TradeCopierEngine.cs:2932, deliberately BEFORE recursion guard 1 drops the execution -- a copy coming back as a follower fill is the only observation the copier ever gets of what its own order actually cost, so the measurement has to hook in ahead of the drop.

`RecordPendingCopy` (:2627) is called at :3134 immediately after a successful `Submit`, with the same Order instance `CreateOrder` returned. That is why the key is right on this path, and why a miss would mean some OTHER path is producing the fill.

`CopierLog` is at :2886 and already forwards to `RiskGuardAddOn.LogFromComponent`, so anything logged here lands in the interventions ledger and in the bridge's event stream -- which is what makes it readable after the fact. The 2026-08-09 exit-mirror failure could not be explained precisely because the dropped path left no trace, and every early return in `OnExecution` was instrumented for that reason. This ticket applies the same treatment one layer down.
